name: Jaguar / Land Rover
description: Jaguar and Land Rover over a generic OBD-II dongle. Honest per-era scope (docs/private/jlr-research-architecture.md): the 2006-2016 Ford/PLA CAN cars (XF X250, XK, Disco 3/4, RR Sport L320, Freelander 2, Ford-era L322, XJ X351, F-Type) answer 11-bit UDS on HS-CAN pins 6/14 -- engine 7E0, ZF gearbox 7E1 and the rear e-diff 795 are the publicly-verified modules; body/comfort modules sit on an MS-CAN not wired to pins 6/14 and are physically unreachable bare. Evoque L538 / Discovery Sport L550 gateway-filter the OBD port (generic OBD only). MY17+ new-architecture cars (Disco 5, Velar, 2018+ Jaguars, Defender L663, I-Pace, L460/L461) moved manufacturer diagnostics to DoIP over Ethernet, which no ELM327 can speak -- generic OBD-II only. Early S-Type/X-Type (J1850) and BMW-era L322 (2002-05) are out of scope. The service resets are dash procedures and work on EVERY era, including the DoIP cars.

panel.title: JLR modules (OBD dongle)
panel.hint: Module scan for Jaguar / Land Rover over the ordinary OBD dongle. Reads the VIN first, then the modules a dongle genuinely reaches on a 2006-2016 CAN-era JLR: engine, ZF automatic gearbox and (where fitted) the rear e-diff, laddering UDS then KWP2000-over-CAN for the older cars. This is an honest engine + driveline read, NOT a full SDD/Pathfinder walk: body modules (BCM, cluster, HVAC, doors) sit on a separate MS-CAN that isn't wired to the OBD pins the dongle uses, air suspension and ABS use module addresses that were never published, and MY17+ cars (Disco 5, Velar, 2018+ Jaguars, Defender L663, I-Pace) do manufacturer diagnostics over DoIP/Ethernet -- generic OBD only. Evoque L538 / Disco Sport L550 gateway-filter the port. The Service tab's dash-procedure resets work on every era, dongle or not. Pick the adapter top-right, ignition ON, then scan.
panel.scanBusy: Walking the JLR driveline modules on 11-bit CAN (engine, gearbox, e-diff)… (absent modules time out quietly)

actions.label: Live extras
actions.title: JLR live extras
actions.hint: Reads JLR-specific values the generic list doesn't carry -- engine oil temperature, measured oil level in mm and calculated oil volume (the dipstick-less cars carry these), boost, post-intercooler charge temp, ZF gearbox oil temperature and rear e-diff oil temperature. Captured from an on-car X351/XK PID pack (petrol AJ133/AJ126; 'should also work' on the diesels), single-source -- verify the scaling against the car. On a car that answers none of them (DoIP-era or gateway-filtered) it falls back to a curated generic Mode-01 set.

actions.label: Find modules
actions.busy: Sweeping the JLR diagnostic address block…
actions.title: Find this car's modules
actions.hint: Sweeps the 0x700-0x7FF request-id block one address at a time (response = request + 8, the verified JLR convention) with a quick presence probe, and reads identification from whatever answers. This is how the never-published module map gets built car by car -- on the X260 3.0d it answers whether a separate SCR/reagent controller exists, and it re-verifies the PCM/TCM addresses the shipped table claims. No fault services, no writes: presence probes and identification only. Takes roughly 2-5 minutes over Bluetooth; absent addresses cost one short timeout each.

actions.label: DID sweep
actions.busy: Walking the DID range, keeping every answer raw…
actions.title: Map this module's DIDs
actions.hint: Walks a 0x22 DID range on one module -- set the range and target in the fields above -- one id at a time, keeping every raw answer. Ranges worth walking on a 306DT diesel PCM (7E0): 0300-05FF and F400-F4FF, where the L494's 191 live DIDs actually are; and D900-D9FF / DE00-DEFF, where SDD 169 names the EGR and turbo valve offsets (D910-D915, DE03-DE05), the high-pressure pump wear (DE02) and the particulate-filter regeneration statistics (DE10/DE11) -- SDD-named for this engine and never yet asked for on a car. Do NOT sweep 2100-21FF or 2200-22FF: all 512 ids refused NRC 31 on the L494 and SDD puts no diesel-PCM identifiers there either. NRC 0x31 refusals are counted (the module is listening, the id isn't implemented); other NRCs are named; the rest are silent. Identify a value by sweeping at idle and again warm/loaded and seeing which payloads MOVE -- nothing is decoded until it has been captured on the car. The target must answer a presence probe or the sweep refuses. Read-only.

actions.label: AdBlue / DPF health
actions.busy: Reading faults, baseline and aftertreatment values…
actions.title: AdBlue / SCR + DPF health (X260 3.0d)
actions.hint: One read-only pass built for the 2016 XF 3.0d: Mode-01 baseline first, the known-table modules' fault codes through the UDS/KWP scan ladder, the known engine DIDs raw with their provenance marked, and a sourced assessment -- the ranked AdBlue fault space (crystallised DEF injector, NOx sensor, tank level sensor, contaminated fluid) and the regen thresholds (auto ~26 g soot, forced permissible below ~46 g, above that a physical clean). Honest gap: no public JLR DID exists for soot mass / DEF level / NOx ppm, so those are flagged capture-pending until the DID sweep maps them on the real car -- no number is invented.

actions.label: SDD dealer data
actions.title: SDD 169 dealer data (L494 MY16 / 306DT diesel)
actions.hint: What Jaguar Land Rover's own dealer database says about this family, decrypted from SDD 169 and shown without a car attached. Three things: the 57-module L494 MY16 CAN address map, which is what lets the module sweep print ABS at 0x7E6 and DSM at 0x744 instead of a bare id; the 37 diesel-PCM data identifiers with SDD's own names, byte sizes, scaling and units; and the 24 PCM/SCR routine identifiers -- including the SCR prime and the three reductant dosing tests -- listed for reference only, because the harness sends none of them. Rows marked [candidate] carry an authoritative SDD name against a value this car has not proved: SDD publishes no scaling for the urea cluster 05FA-05FD, so those stay raw. SDD names a curated 37 of the ~191 DIDs the PCM answers, so absence here does not mean a DID is dead. No car contact at all -- this reads the same with the dongle unplugged.

actions.label: AdBlue drive log
actions.busy: Logging rpm against the aftertreatment DIDs…
actions.title: AdBlue / DPF drive log
actions.hint: A timed log pairing engine rpm with the AdBlue/DPF candidate DIDs -- set the length above (a regen is ~20 min at 500 °C+, so give it the seconds; the backend saves every real run to captures/jlr/ and the CSV button appears after). Every tick reads rpm plus each DID's RAW payload with a timestamp, every fifth tick adds coolant and module voltage, and the achieved sample rate is reported. Payloads stay raw on purpose: a signal is identified by how it moves against rpm, then decoded against the car. Default DIDs are the known engine set; paste sweep-captured candidates (comma-separated hex) to log those instead, or press a watch preset to load a short focused list. Read-only.

presets.label: Full candidate set
presets.note: The Old Jaguar Group engine DIDs plus every live external candidate -- the broad default when you do not yet know what you are chasing. Slowest per-DID sample rate, widest coverage.

presets.label: DPF + EGR (sweep candidates)
presets.note: The six aftertreatment-shaped candidates the 2026-08-18 L494 sweep found live (F40C leading), logged on their own for a higher sample rate. None is decoded and SDD names none of them: the job is to see which payload MOVES like soot, EGR or EGT between idle and warm/loaded. A regen needs ~20 min at 500 °C+, so give it the seconds to span one.

presets.label: Urea / SCR 05FA-05FD
presets.note: The next real-world step on the L494. Four SDD-named, PCM-managed urea identifiers polled on their own, so each samples fast enough to be calibrated. Drive it WARM -- reagent dosing only starts once the SCR catalyst is up to temperature, so a cold log records four constants. 05FC is 'total mass fluid injected by the urea dosing system', a monotonic total: the rate it climbs is what pins the scaling SDD does not publish.
